did_you_know.text: Psalm 128 opens with the heading “A Song of Ascents” and presents reverence for the Lord and walking in his ways as the foundation of a blessed life.
The verse defines a blessed person not by wealth or status, but by reverence for the Lord and the way he lives.
The blessing is also expressed through the fruit of one’s labor: a person eats from the work of his hands, and the verse describes this as happiness and prosperity.
The family is described using images from nature: the wife is compared to a fruitful vine, and the sons to olive shoots.
The sons are pictured sitting around the table, emphasizing the home and the family meal as places of closeness and blessing.
The verse sums up the preceding description with a general statement: this is how the man who reveres the Lord is blessed.
The blessing is not limited to the home; it extends from Zion to Jerusalem, and the person is called to see Jerusalem’s prosperity all the days of his life.
The height of the blessing is continuity across generations: seeing one’s children’s children—that is, grandchildren—and, alongside this, a prayer for peace upon Israel.
